current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance becomes eligible -> free/standard settlement ETA and paid speed tiers are known -> external bank liquidity and obligations due before each ETA determine actual shortfall -> recommend zero, next-day, same-day, or instant settlement and only the minimum amount -> verify acceleration fees avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Fresh searches found strong evidence that instant payouts remain materially priced and are intended for selective urgent liquidity rather than routine use. Yoco charges roughly 1%-1.5% plus VAT depending on plan and explicitly tells merchants to request the amount they need; MeevoPay Now charges 1.75%; Stripe-linked Dubsado currently lists 1%-1.5% by country; Cashfree starts at 0.30%. Stripe also supports daily, weekly, monthly, and manual payout schedules. No exact product was found that combines PSP balance/ETA, paid speed tiers, live bank cash, and obligations to compute the minimum economically necessary accelerated amount. Exact avoidable-volume evidence is still missing, so leakage remains uncertain rather than passed.
current_leader.closest_threat: First parties already expose amount selection, payout schedules, and speed choices, while banks/treasury products aggregate cash. Novo even offers fee-free faster Stripe access for eligible customers, which economically neutralizes the wedge for that subset. Gate 8 remains uncertain until exact cross-system cash-aware minimum-acceleration decisioning is ruled out comprehensively.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP available/instant-eligible balance, standard settlement ETA, paid speed tiers, bank balance and obligations due before standard settlement. Output the cheapest sufficient choice and minimum amount. V1 does not initiate a payout or hold funds.
current_leader.monetization: Small per valuable settlement decision, low recurring micro-fee, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided versus a competent treasury baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: There is still no reliable primary evidence quantifying how much paid accelerated-settlement volume is unnecessary after accounting for genuine liquidity needs. If merchants already accelerate selectively, the recoverable fee pool may be too small.
current_leader.next_research_test: Search processor disclosures, merchant surveys, payment-company filings or anonymized transaction studies quantifying instant/same-day payout adoption and merchant liquidity need. Estimate actual acceleration fees minus minimum fees required to avoid genuine shortfalls. In parallel search treasury/banking products for exact PSP-balance + bank-balance + obligations + settlement-fee decisioning. Kill if avoidable volume is immaterial or exact functionality is found.

recent_cross_family_findings: Merchant settlement acceleration remains current leader at 46/60. Instant payout products remain materially priced and are explicitly framed for selective liquidity use, but primary evidence of avoidable over-acceleration remains missing.
Per-shipment insurance selection is rejected on Gate 8: Insurrl already makes the exact per-order skip/use-carrier/route-to-insurer decision with store/API integrations and savings attribution.

Music royalty underpayment recovery is rejected on Gate 8: PointsOwl already performs contract-and-statement royalty audits on a 20% success fee, while RoyaltyCoPilot, SongBounty and CheckMyRoyalty cover adjacent leakage/underpayment recovery workflows.
Corporate gift-card breakage tracking is rejected for the basic wedge: CardLockr already provides expiry alerts, balance tracking, APIs/webhooks and team controls.

Novo's fee-free Stripe Boost demonstrates that first-party/banking alternatives can economically neutralize paid-acceleration optimization for subsets even without copying the exact decision algorithm.
New search rule: primary behavioral evidence is required before recurring leakage can move from UNCERTAIN to PASS for optional paid-speed products.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
